sum_PrimePow_eq_sum_sum

  ∑ n ∈ Ioc 0 ⌊x⌋₊ with IsPrimePow n, f n =
    ∑ k ∈ Icc 1 ⌊log x / log 2⌋₊, ∑ p ∈ Ioc 0 ⌊x ^ ((1 : ℝ) / k)⌋₊ with p.Prime, f (p ^ k)

result.informal_description: For any additive commutative monoid $R$, function $f : \mathbb{N} \to R$, and real number $x \geq 0$, the sum of $f(n)$ over all prime powers $n$ in the interval $(0, \lfloor x \rfloor]$ equals the double sum over $k \in [1, \lfloor \log x / \log 2 \rfloor]$ and primes $p$ in $(0, \lfloor x^{1/k} \rfloor]$ of $f(p^k)$. That is, $$\sum_{\substack{n \in (0, \lfloor x \rfloor] \\ n \text{ prime power}}} f(n) = \sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor \log x / \log 2 \rfloor} \sum_{\substack{p \in (0, \lfloor x^{1/k} \rfloor] \\ p \text{ prime}}} f(p^k).$$

name: ArithmeticFunction
sigma_apply
result.signature: {k n : ℕ} : σ k n = ∑ d ∈ divisors n, d ^ k
result.type: ∀ {k n : ℕ}, (ArithmeticFunction.sigma k) n = ∑ d ∈ n.divisors, d ^ k
result.informal_name: Sigma Function Applied to Natural Number: Sum of Divisors to the k-th Power
result.informal_description: For any natural numbers $k$ and $n$, the value of the arithmetic function $\sigma_k(n)$ is equal to the sum of $d^k$ over all positive divisors $d$ of $n$, i.e., $\sigma_k(n) = \sum_{d \mid n} d^k$.

result.informal_description: For any natural number $k$ and element $r$ in a nontrivially normed field $\mathbb{K}$ with $\|r\| < 1$, the double infinite sum $\sum_{d=1}^\infty \sum_{c=1}^\infty c^k r^{dc}$ equals the single infinite sum $\sum_{e=1}^\infty \sigma_k(e) r^e$, where $\sigma_k(e)$ denotes the sum of $d^k$ over all positive divisors $d$ of $e$.

result.informal_name: Sigma Function for Divisors to the k-th Power
result.informal_description: For a natural number $ k $, the function $ \sigma_k $ maps each natural number $ n $ to the sum of $ d^k $ over all divisors $ d $ of $ n $. Since $ \sigma_k(0) = 0 $, it qualifies as an arithmetic function.

name: Chebyshev
eventually_primeCounting_le
result.signature: {ε : ℝ} (εpos : 0 < ε) : ∀ᶠ x in atTop, π ⌊x⌋₊ ≤ (log 4 + ε) * x / log x
result.type: ∀ {ε : ℝ}, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, ↑⌊x⌋₊.primeCounting ≤ (Real.log 4 + ε) * x / Real.log x
result.value:
:= by
  have := integral_theta_div_log_sq_isLittleO.bound εpos
  filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop 2, this] with x hx hx2
  rw [primeCounting_eq_theta_div_log_add_integral hx, add_mul, add_div]
  have hl : 0 ≤ log x := by bound
  rw [norm_of_nonneg (show 0 ≤ x / log x by bound), ← mul_div_assoc] at hx2
  grw [theta_le_log4_mul_x (by linarith), ← hx2]
  grind [le_norm_self]
result.informal_description: For any positive real number $\varepsilon$, there exists some $X$ such that for all $x \geq X$, the prime-counting function $\pi(\lfloor x \rfloor)$ satisfies $\pi(\lfloor x \rfloor) \leq \frac{(\log 4 + \varepsilon)x}{\log x}$.
